snippet.title: Venezuela earthquake: How long can trapped victims survive under rubble? - BBC World Service
snippet.description:
After a devastating double earthquake in Venezuela, tens of thousands of people are still believed to be missing, with many trapped under rubble. 

Click here to subscribe to our channel 👉🏽 https://bbc.in/3VyyriM

Nearly 1,500 people have been confirmed dead and the death toll is expected to rise. Aid agencies say the first 72 hours after a disaster are the most critical to finding people alive. But there is a lack of heavy machinery and specialised equipment needed to rescue people. Much of the emergency response is being carried out by volunteers and international aid workers from Turkey, the UK and France. BBC’s Global Affairs reporter Mimi Swaby gives us the latest update on the situation.

Against all odds, several videos online show miraculous stories of survival, like young infants and children being lifted from the rubble. Bill Murphy, a professor of engineering geology at the University of Leeds in the UK, tells us what increases the chances of survival in awful conditions like these.

snippet.title: 'THEY LIED ABOUT TRUMP'
snippet.description:
I've been waiting 10 years to ask someone these questions, and today I finally get to do that.

Ever since I was a kid, I’ve been fascinated by American politics. Back then, I used to watch the elections, every interview and all the debates from my bedroom, trying to figure out why a system thousands of miles away felt so consequential to my life.

So when I was given the chance to have a sit-down conversation with Vice President Of The United States JD Vance, I knew I didn’t just want to ask him about headlines.

I wanted to understand the person behind the headlines.

At the start of the conversation, I said to him: “To understand the people that are sitting in front of me, you have to get a picture of their early context.”

And the reality is, I didn't truly know his context…

What I really wanted to find out by speaking with VP is: How much of what people think they know about VP Vance is ACTUALLY true?

Long before he entered the White House, VP grew up in a home shaped by addiction, poverty, instability, and a revolving door of father figures.

I went into this conversation wanting to understand how a kid raised in addiction and instability became the Vice President of the United States. And then get to the bottom of what he really thinks about everything happening in the world right now with no questions left unsaid.

We spoke about:

- The childhood instability that shaped the way he sees people.
- The conversation that changed his view of Donald Trump.
- His return to Christianity after years as an atheist.
- Whether he wants to be President one day.
- The immigration debate that is dividing America.
- Why doesn't he trust the UK Government?
- Whether he thinks aliens exist…
- When will a proposed ceasefire deal with Iran happen?
- Navigating one of the most demanding jobs on earth while raising a young family.

One of the things that I've come to learn is just try and meet everybody as I experience them.

Regardless of where you stand politically, this conversation goes deeper than politics.

And as a podcaster, having these conversations is important, as it goes beyond the headlines and shows you how the people in power actually think.

snippet.title: The Moment AI Started Thinking And Nobody Noticed It Happening #ai
snippet.description:
What if the biggest moment in the history of artificial intelligence didn't happen in a laboratory, on a stage, or during a major announcement?

What if it happened quietly... and almost nobody noticed?

For decades, computers followed instructions. They calculated, processed, and executed commands exactly as they were programmed. But at some point, something changed. AI systems stopped simply responding and began demonstrating behaviors that looked surprisingly similar to reasoning, planning, problem-solving, and even creativity.

In this video, we explore the fascinating journey that led to the moment AI appeared to cross an invisible threshold. Was it a sudden breakthrough, or the result of countless small advances that accumulated over time? We'll examine the evolution of neural networks, the rise of large language models, emergent abilities, and the growing debate among scientists, engineers, and philosophers about whether AI is truly "thinking" or merely creating the illusion of thought.

From early experiments to the most advanced AI systems of today, this story reveals how one of the most important technological shifts in human history unfolded right before our eyes—and why so few people realized it was happening.

The future may have arrived more quietly than anyone expected.

📌 Watch until the end to discover why the question isn't whether AI is getting smarter but how far its capabilities can go.
